text:
Ibrahim: Kickoff note — we need a compact battlecard and two benchmark blurbs for LaunchCraft. Focus: positioning vs cloud-managed endpoints and infra vendors. Keep everything one page for SDRs.

Sophie: High-level asks: 3 crisp claims, 3 micro-rebuttals, 2 bench storylines (no heavy numbers in hero), and a tiny paste-ready routing example.

Claire: Suggested claim set (dev-friendly wording):
- "Same API, different guarantees" (emphasize unified surface but multiple deployment guarantees)
- "Workload-aware economics" (call out batching + caching + quantization as levers)
- "Operational SLAs + graceful fallbacks" (stress routing & rollback)

Tom: Micro-rebuttals (30s lines):
- "We use cloud endpoints" -> "Keep those endpoints; Redwood gives a single runtime, rollout controls, and per-route cost traces."
- "We care about compliance" -> "Private control plane, KMS + audit trail, and deploys that fit your network model."
- "We can't accept regressions" -> "Built-in evals and canary rollouts reduce risk and make rollbacks safe."

Ibrahim: Bench storylines (short):
- Chat-first SaaS: steady token throughput; outcome: batching + KV caching reduces unit tail cost and stabilizes p95. Method: replay of production prompt set, real token distribution.
- Burst analytics ingest: spiky arrival, variable sequence lengths; outcome: routing policies + prewarmed pools keep availability; method: staged spike tests + canary-induced failure to demo fallback.

Sophie: Webinar plan (tight): 3m setup, 7m methodology, 10m scripted demo (failover + canary swap), 15m customer stories panel, 5m CTA. Demo must intentionally trigger a fallback so SDRs can see the script.

Claire: Email subject A/B ideas (short):
- A: "Stop firefighting inference: predictable costs & fallbacks"
- B: "Manage LLM inference across hosted, reserved, and private"
- C: "Ship LLM features with predictable economics"

Tom: Inbound routing/Intercom rules: create tags = [demo, enterprise-dedicated, technical-eval]. Automation: enterprise-dedicated -> assign to solutions-eng + high-touch SDR; technical-eval -> send bench notebook + invite to private eval channel. Add UTM-based scoring to bump priority.

Ibrahim: Battlecard sketch bullets for SDRs:
- Elevator (15s): "Redwood lets you run models where you need them with rollout controls and cost/latency transparency."
- 30s pitch: follow the claims + 1 line customer example.
- Demo script: short steps to trigger rollback in demo environment and the lines to say on the call.

Sophie: Paste-ready routing snippet for playbook:
```
# simple routing pseudo
policy = load_policy(customer_id)
if policy.reserved_capacity < policy.min_threshold:
    forward(req, variant='hosted_compat', tags=['fallback'])
    notify_team('fallback_triggered')
else:
    forward(req, variant='reserved_primary')
```

Claire: Also include 'how we differ' bullets to counter infra vendors: no need to rebuild orchestration (we provide runtime + compilation + routing) and to counter cloud APIs: more operational controls and private deployment options.

Tom: Logistics: landing page created by events-bot -> /events/launchcraft; recording room reserved Thu 9:30 PT. Need deck + one-pager by Tue noon; SDR battlecard + Intercom flows by Thu EOD.

events-bot: Landing page created -> /events/launchcraft; recording slot booked Thu 09:30 PT.
Ibrahim: Assignments: Sophie -> hero copy + email A/B; Claire -> bench blurbs + 'how we differ' bullets; Tom -> Intercom flows + SDR one-pager template. I'll assemble and drop the first draft into #marketing-drafts by Tue PM. Keep messages short in the doc. :sparkles:
